actTools.intro: Learn six hand tools, match each one to a job, practice knowing when to stop and get help, then use a tape measure and a level.

hammer.name: Claw hammer
hammer.use: Drives nails in. The curved claw pulls them out.
hammer.grip: Hold near the end of the handle. Start with light taps.
hammer.safe: Keep your other hand clear and wear eye protection.

phillips.name: Phillips screwdriver
phillips.use: Turns screws with a + shaped slot.
phillips.grip: Push in firmly while you turn so it doesn’t slip.
phillips.safe: Righty-tighty, lefty-loosey. Keep your free hand out of its path.

tape.name: Tape measure
tape.use: Measures length, width and height in inches and feet.
tape.grip: Hook the end on the edge, pull the tape straight.
tape.safe: Let it roll back slowly. A fast snap-back can pinch fingers.

wrench.name: Adjustable wrench
wrench.use: Grips nuts and bolts of different sizes.
wrench.grip: Roll the little wheel until the jaw is snug on the nut.
wrench.safe: Pull toward you rather than pushing, so your knuckles stay safe if it slips.

flat.name: Flathead screwdriver
flat.use: Turns screws with one straight slot.
flat.grip: Match the blade width to the slot.
flat.safe: It isn’t a pry bar. Prying can snap the tip.

level.name: Level
level.use: Shows if something is straight. Bubble centered means level.
level.grip: Rest it flat on the top edge of what you’re checking.
level.safe: For heavy items like shelves, have a partner hold while you check.

jobs: Your new bookshelf is 30 inches wide. Will it fit next to your desk?
A cabinet handle wobbles. Its screw has a + shaped slot.
You hung a frame and it looks a little crooked. How can you check?
The nut on a bike seat clamp is loose. What grips it and turns it?
With an adult nearby, you’re tapping in a small picture-hanging nail.
A toy’s battery cover is held by a screw with one straight slot.
actTools.stopSkill: Knowing when to stop is a real skill. You just practiced it six times.
actTools.rule: The rule to remember: water spreading, electricity, gas, or anything that feels unsafe means get an adult first.
actTools.someJobs: Some jobs are yours. Some need an adult. Some need a professional, fast.

prop.s: The toilet keeps running and water is starting to drip onto the floor.
prop.why: Tell an adult right away. They can turn the small valve behind the toilet to stop the water. You can help by finding it and grabbing towels.

prop.s: A picture frame in your room is hanging crooked.
prop.why: You can handle this one. Use the level, nudge the frame until the bubble is centered, and you’re done.

prop.s: You smell something like rotten eggs in the kitchen, and the stove is off.
prop.why: That smell can mean a gas leak. Don’t flip any switches. Get everyone outside, then call 911 or the gas company from outside.

prop.s: An outlet near your desk sparked and popped when you plugged in a charger.
prop.why: Stop using it and tell an adult. Outlets and wiring are jobs for an adult or an electrician, never a quick fix.

prop.s: Your bike seat is loose and slides down when you sit on it.
prop.why: You can handle this. Snug the clamp nut with the adjustable wrench, and check that it’s tight before you ride.

prop.s: Water is coming through the ceiling during a storm.
prop.why: Tell an adult immediately and stay away from outlets or lights near the water. A roof leak needs a professional.

prop.s: A kitchen cabinet door hangs loose because one hinge screw backed out.
prop.why: You can handle this one. Hold the door straight and snug the screw with the Phillips screwdriver. If the screw just spins, tell an adult.

prop.s: The batteries in the TV remote died.
prop.why: You can handle this. Slide the cover off, match the plus and minus marks, and put the old batteries where your family keeps used ones.

prop.s: The kitchen sink drains slowly and smells a little.
prop.why: Tell an adult. Drain cleaners are harsh chemicals, and taking the pipe apart is an adult job. You can help by keeping food scraps out of the sink.

prop.s: The smoke alarm in the hallway chirps every minute.
prop.why: Tell an adult today. A chirp means the battery is low, and alarms matter too much to skip. You can help by pointing out which one it is.

prop.s: A power line is down in the yard after a storm.
prop.why: Stay far away, even if it looks dead. Keep everyone and pets inside, and tell an adult to call 911 or the power company.

prop.s: The furnace is banging loudly and the house smells like something burning.
prop.why: Tell an adult right away, and get out of the house if the smell is strong. A furnace is a job for a professional, never a quick fix.

actTools.question: Question {n} of 4
actTools.tapeQ: Where does the edge of the board land on the tape?
actTools.tapeGroup: What length does the tape show?
actTools.readTapeP: You are looking at 3 inches of tape, zoomed in. Find the big number just before the red line, then count the small marks past it. Each small mark is 1/16 inch.
actTools.shelfQ: Tilt the shelf until the bubble sits between the two lines.
actTools.levelP: A bubble level shows which side is higher. The bubble floats to the high side. Move the slider or use the arrow keys, and stop when the bubble sits between the lines.
actTools.levelFbP: That’s how you hang a shelf straight.
actTools.usedBoth: You read the tape and leveled the shelf.
